title: Routing synthesis engine: refactor to modular rule synthesis with explicit schema validation
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Refactor the policy routing engine into a modular 'synthesis' pipeline that compiles high-level routing rules (region selectors, tier preferences, fallback model variants) into a typed intermediate representation (IR) with an explicit, versioned schema. The goal is to make validation deterministically checkable, enable staged rollouts of new rule primitives, and improve observability of rule decisions for SLO-sensitive paths. This work includes: (1) a backwards-compatible parser that accepts existing DSL configs and emits the new IR, (2) a strict schema validator with clear error messages and autofix suggestions, (3) a runtime compatibility shim for canary rollouts, and (4) telemetry hooks to score fallback choices and region selection decisions for later tuning.
acceptance_criteria: New synthesis pipeline accepts 100% of existing production rule sets (via compatibility parser) and emits IR that can be executed by both old and new dispatchers in shadow mode
Schema validator enforces typed fields, rejects ambiguous selectors (e.g., overlapping region/tier constraints) with actionable error messages and suggested edits
Unit and property tests cover compilation of region selectors, tier weights, and fallback chains with >90% mutation coverage for the rule compiler module
Canary rollout plan implemented: 5% traffic to new engine for two weeks with automated rollback on error-rate or 95th latency regression beyond thresholds
Telemetry dashboard surfaces per-rule decision frequency, fallback activation counts, and step-by-step evaluation traces for three sample apps
Migration tool (autofix) produces a safe patch for at least 80% of rules that previously failed validation and outputs a human-reviewable diff for the remainder
tasks: Design typed IR and versioned schema (proto/spec)
Implement compatibility parser that translates legacy DSL AST -> IR
Build schema validator library with detailed diagnostics and autofix engine
Add runtime shim to allow dual-execution (old dispatcher + new synthesized dispatcher) in shadow mode
Integrate telemetry hooks and create initial Grafana/Console dashboards
Write unit, integration, and property tests; add mutation tests for compiler
Prepare migration assistant and canary rollout runbook
Create PRD and run cross-team review with Console/Infra/PM/Design
notes: Decision: choose a compact IR that is language-agnostic (JSON + typed fields) rather than protobuf to keep developer debugging simple; versioning via schema_version field
Trade-off: strict validation improves safety but will surface many historical config smells; autofix aims to reduce manual edit surface but must be conservative
Compatibility approach: graceful fallback — if new IR cannot represent a legacy construct, emit a compatibility-annotation and route that rule through legacy dispatcher until manual migration
Performance: synthesized rules should not add more than 2% CPU overhead at 99th percentile path; we will microbenchmark rule evaluation and cache compiled predicates
Telemetry: attach per-decision trace IDs so we can correlate routing choices with downstream SLO signals in Console
Security: no new secrets; schema validation runs in control plane. If future work touches customer-sensitive selectors, route review through Security
